title: fix(console): the catalog's org install waits until its app is served before refreshing (objectui#12097)
body:
Fixes #12097
Clause-②: yes

## What changed

On a cloud-managed environment, the catalog page's org install (`doOrgInstall` in `packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/MarketplacePage.tsx`) sent `emitMetadataRefresh()` the moment `installPackage` answered. That answer lands inside the runtime's stale-while-rebuild window, so every mounted `MetadataProvider` re-read and persisted the pre-install `app` list. This is the package-page defect from objectui#12087, on the "Your organization" Install button.

- **The wait.** The cloud branch now calls the one `waitForServedApp` from objectui#12096, unchanged, with the row's `manifest_id`. It sends the pulse only once an app whose `_packageId` is that manifest id is served. There is no second copy of the wait: the interval and the bound are the module's defaults (`SERVED_APP_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`, `SERVED_APP_WAIT_CAP_MS`). As on the package page, the wait is not awaited and not cancelled on unmount.
- **What the strip says.** A status box at the top of the strip, above the package cards, carries the installed package's name and the package page's three states in the package page's words: `marketplace.install.deploying` while it waits; `marketplace.install.deployed` plus `marketplace.install.openApp` once the app is served; `marketplace.install.deployTimeout` plus `marketplace.install.checkAgain` when the wait expires. The cloud branch no longer says `marketplace.org.installed` ("Installed NAME") before the app is served, and on expiry it refreshes nothing.
- **One status for the whole strip.** A later install's status replaces an earlier one's. An earlier wait that settles late never overwrites the later status, but its pulse still goes out, because its app is served.
- **The `installLocal` branch is unchanged.** The runtime hot-registers the package before it answers, so the strip says "Installed NAME" and pulses at once, as before. The test pins this as its CONTROL.

## Measured before building (the dispatch's mechanism assumptions)

1. **On `main`, the cloud branch refreshes at once: confirmed.** The new pin fails against `main`'s `MarketplacePage.tsx` (base `5330afd1f`). The bus carried one pulse at virtual t=0, and at that point the runtime was not serving the app yet:
   - `AssertionError: expected [ { at: +0, served: false } ] to deeply equal []`
   - `Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)`. The CONTROL is green on `main`.
2. **`waitForServedApp` can be called unchanged with the row's `manifest_id`: confirmed at the producer.**
   - The "Your organization" rows come from the runtime proxy `GET /api/v1/cloud-connection/org-packages` in objectstack `packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts`. That proxy passes the control plane's `items` through unchanged.
   - The control plane builds each row in cloud `packages/service-cloud/src/routes/package-publish.ts` (`GET /cloud/org-packages`) as `manifest_id: p.manifest_id` from `sys_package`. That field is declared `required: true` and `readonly: true` in cloud `packages/service-tenant/src/objects/sys-package.object.ts`.
   - `OrgPackageSummary.manifest_id` is already a required `string`. No fallback was added. The `installLocal` branch's `pkg.manifest_id || pkg.id` is untouched.
3. **The package page's copy is reusable, so no locale key is added.** The five `marketplace.install` keys from objectui#12096 say exactly what this install's states mean. The one thing the catalog adds is which package the status is about, because the strip lists several packages and the status sits above them all. That is supplied as the row's display name, drawn as the status box's title (the same raw `display_name` the org card already renders), not by a second, NAME-carrying copy of each sentence in ten packs. The meaning is shared and the copy is shared, so the two pages cannot drift. `@object-ui/i18n` does not move and the changeset declares `@object-ui/app-shell` patch only.

## Route versus the suggested one

The dispatch suggested mirroring the package page's "drop the seed, `refreshMetadata()`, pulse". This PR keeps the catalog page's own post-install action, the pulse, and moves it behind the wait. This page did not drop the seed or call `refreshMetadata()` before, and the pulse already makes every mounted provider refresh and re-persist, this page's own included. Adding those two would be a second behaviour change beyond the card's scope, which is "Before the pulse, the org install waits on `waitForServedApp`". The test asserts on the seed the real provider writes: after the install, no `app` seed write ever lacks the installed app.

## Clause-②

- Exports added: none. The `@object-ui/app-shell` entry's exports, props and types are unchanged, and `MarketplacePage` keeps its signature.
- Locale keys added: none, in all ten packs. The page reads five existing `marketplace.install` keys (`deploying`, `deployed`, `deployTimeout`, `openApp`, `checkAgain`).
- `Clause-②: yes` stays as the claim declared it, for the seat's contract review to record.

## Evidence (head `b32312a`)

- **Test on the virtual clock.** `MarketplacePage.orgInstallWaitServed-12097.test.tsx` runs the real `waitForServedApp` at its real interval and bound. Only `now` and `sleep` are swapped, and the test opens each sleep one interval at a time. It mounts the real `MetadataProvider` and the real assistant bus over a runtime that serves the pre-install list for 60 s of virtual time after the install.
  - **Stale window:** after each of the eleven stale intervals there is no pulse and no pre-install seed write. At 60 s there is exactly one pulse, with the app served, plus "Open Acme CRM".
  - **Expiry:** after 60 intervals the clock reads exactly `SERVED_APP_WAIT_CAP_MS`. The status reads `deployTimeout`, with no pulse, no success and no seed write. "Check again" finds the app on its first read.
  - **CONTROL:** `installLocal` pulses at once, starts no wait and says "Installed Acme CRM".
- **Ablation (fix committed, then mutated with automatic restore).**
  - Made with `ablation-replace.mjs`, which replaced the wait call with `emitMetadataRefresh();`. Anchor count went 1 to 0, and the blob went `b3073eed036d` to `244d714449af`.
  - Result: `Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)`. The two waits are red and the CONTROL is green.
  - Restored: the blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Gates.**
  - `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exit 0. The output echoes `type-check`, and `--listFilesOnly` confirms that `tsconfig.test.json` covers the new test file.
  - `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/ packages/i18n/src/__tests__/marketplace-preview-namespace-3546.test.tsx`: `Test Files 28 passed (28)`, `Tests 222 passed (222)`. The i18n file reads this page's source.
  - Every `check:*` gate the dispatch named exited 0, plus `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check:unreferenced-sources` and `check-governed-queue-guard --test` (NOT GOVERNED).
- **Eager closure.** Built with `vite build` for base and head, on the same tree except `MarketplacePage.tsx`.
  - Base and head both measure 3170.2 KB gzipped across 290 of 2474 chunks. The delta is -1 byte, and `MarketplacePage` is in no eager chunk.
  - `check:eager-closure` and `check:eager-locale-catalogues` both exit 0.
- **Narrowed lint.**
  - eslint over the 2 touched source files (counted from `--format json`): 0 errors and 2 warnings. Both warnings are pre-existing, and the base file shows the same two rules.
  - The population and the invariance come from eslint's own `--print-config` for both files: `parserOptions` is empty, so type-aware linting is off and this diff cannot change the verdict on any untouched file.
  - Repo-wide `pnpm lint` belongs to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- The `readApps` closure is the same three lines as the package page's. A shared reader would edit `MarketplacePackagePage.tsx` or `waitForServedApp.ts`, which is outside this claim. Carrier: objectui#12098, which edits around `waitForServedApp.ts`. #12098 is not addressed here, and this page inherits its version-aware predicate if it lands in `waitForServedApp`.
- Refs: #12087, #12096.
